## Methods

### Overview and implementation

All analyses were performed with a custom, portable workflow implemented in Nextflow DSL2 (≥23.04; @ditommaso2017) and run on an HPC cluster under the SLURM scheduler.

The workflow comprises a one-time reference-construction stage followed by a per-sample pipeline: SRA discovery → FASTQ download → quality control → Kraken2 papillomavirus screen → branch on HPV status (only HPV-positive libraries proceed) → STAR alignment to the HPV reference panel → coverage-based HPV typing → early/late transcript classification → aggregation and reporting.

### HPV reference panel and Kraken2 database

A cutaneous-inclusive HPV reference panel was assembled from the Papillomavirus Episteme (PaVE 2.0; @vandoorslaer2017). Reference-quality complete HPV genomes from NCBI RefSeq were added on a best-effort basis via Entrez Direct (≥16.2; `"Human papillomavirus"[Organism] AND refseq[filter] AND complete genome[Title]`). Sequences were concatenated and deduplicated by identifier with seqkit ≥2.5 [@shen2016] to yield the final panel (`hpv_all.fasta`; *n* = `r stats$panel_n` genomes spanning the alpha, beta, gamma, mu and nu genera plus unclassified candidate types). Because both sources are updated continuously, the panel is fixed at build time: PaVE and RefSeq were queried on 17 April 2026, and every analysis reported here uses that build. A per-type genus lookup was derived from the PaVE ICTV taxonomy array. Gene models for the eight protein-coding ORFs of interest (E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, L1, L2) were extracted from each genome's PaVE feature annotation, with multi-segment features collapsed to a single span, and written as a GFF3 annotation used downstream for transcript classification.

A STAR genome index was built over the panel (STAR ≥2.7.10; `--genomeSAindexNbases 6` for the small viral genomes). A Kraken2 database (≥2.1.3; @wood2019) was constructed from the NCBI taxonomy and the human reference library (GRCh38), to which all panel HPV genomes were added under a Papillomaviridae taxon, so that human and HPV reads are jointly classified and HPV reads are resolved within the papillomavirus clade.

### Dataset assembly and SRA discovery

Public human RNA-seq libraries were identified by programmatic query of the NCBI Sequence Read Archive through Entrez (Biopython `Bio.Entrez`; pysradb/Biopython container 2.2.1), with every query intersected with a common base filter (`"Homo sapiens"[Organism] AND "RNA-Seq"[Strategy] AND "public"[Access]`). We used three complementary discovery strategies, corresponding to the case/control framing of the study. An unbiased prevalence sweep of human skin and related tissues (the prevalence cohort) estimated baseline HPV-positivity rates in tissue not selected for infection. A targeted productive-lesion query (epidermodysplasia verruciformis, verruca/warts, condyloma) provided positive controls of known productive cutaneous HPV infection. A broadened skin-neoplasia query additionally captured cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, actinic keratosis and Bowen disease alongside the wider wart/papilloma vocabulary, to interrogate HPV across the AK-to-cSCC setting.

For each retrieved run, metadata were parsed into a per-run samplesheet (one row per SRR). A tissue category was assigned by longest-keyword-first matching of sample title and source fields against a curated keyword table, yielding one of four classes: skin, anogenital, oral, or unclassified (the default, meaning no site keyword was present rather than a site outside the other three). Keywords are matched with letter boundaries on both sides, tolerating a plural suffix, so that a keyword is not matched inside an unrelated word; the boundary is letter-based rather than word-based because SRA free text routinely separates tokens with underscores and digits. Squamous- and basal-cell-carcinoma abbreviations are exempt from the boundary rule, since they legitimately take anatomical affixes (cSCC, RDEB-SCC, SCCIS). A free-text diagnosis was extracted against a fixed pathology vocabulary (carcinoma, SCC, BCC, keratosis, wart, verruca, condyloma, epidermodysplasia verruciformis, dysplasia/CIN, normal/healthy/control, and similar terms), defaulting to "unspecified". Library layout (single- vs paired-end) was taken from the SRA record. To enable robust downstream parsing, comma-containing free-text fields were retained in a raw samplesheet and stripped from the slim samplesheet consumed by the workflow.

### Read download and quality control

FASTQ files were retrieved from the SRA [@leinonen2011] with the NCBI SRA Toolkit (3.1.1, pinned; later 3.4.x builds were unstable in our environment) by `prefetch` followed by `fasterq-dump --split-3`, and compressed with pigz. Reads were quality- and adapter-trimmed with fastp (0.23.4; @chen2018) using a minimum qualified base quality of Phred 20 (`--qualified_quality_phred 20`) and a minimum retained read length of 36 nt (`--length_required 36`); paired-end libraries additionally used `--detect_adapter_for_pe`. Single-sample failures (withdrawn accessions, network errors) were retried and then skipped, so one unavailable run did not abort a batch. No step subsampled reads and `fasterq-dump` was run without a spot limit; the reads reaching Kraken2 were a median `r pp(stats$spot_med)`% of the SRA-reported spot count, and `r pp(stats$spot_tier_lo)`% to `r pp(stats$spot_tier_hi)`% across the individual sample groups.

Libraries whose every read fell under the length filter returned no screening result. The main Methods account for those of the untargeted sweep. Of the `r comma(stats$les_submitted)` targeted lesion libraries, `r stats$les_unscr` likewise returned none, all of them length-filtered (read 1 of `r stats$les_unscr_r1lo` to `r stats$les_unscr_r1hi` nt) and none through a failed download. By read geometry, `r stats$les_unscr_pe_short` have two mates of 27 to 28 nt and come from two spatial-profiling studies whose libraries are annotated by area of illumination (SRP413119 and SRP413116); `r stats$les_unscr_bc` pair a 26 to 28 nt barcode read with a cDNA read, the layout of droplet single-cell libraries; and `r stats$les_unscr_se` are 35 nt single-end libraries. Of the `r stats$les_unscr`, `r stats$les_unscr_dx` carried a carcinoma, condyloma or papilloma diagnosis. Both sets are listed with their cause in Supplementary Data.

### HPV screening and positivity calling

Trimmed reads were classified against the combined human+HPV Kraken2 database (≥2.1.3, paired or single mode as appropriate). HPV-classified reads were enumerated as the count of unique read identifiers assigned to the Papillomaviridae family or any papillomavirus genus/type taxon. A library was called HPV-positive when its HPV read count met or exceeded a threshold of 10 reads (`hpv_min_reads = 10`), and HPV-negative otherwise; HPV-negative libraries were recorded for rate estimation but proceeded no further. HPV-classified reads from positive libraries were extracted (seqtk 1.4), keeping paired mates in register, for targeted alignment.

### HPV typing

HPV reads from positive libraries were aligned to the HPV reference panel with STAR (2.7.11b; @dobin2013) in an end-to-end, splice-disabled configuration appropriate for compact viral genomes (`--alignIntronMax 1`, `--alignEndsType EndToEnd`, `--outFilterMismatchNmax 3`), permitting up to 50 multi-mapping locations (`--outFilterMultimapNmax 50`) to accommodate the high sequence similarity among HPV types. Sorted, indexed BAMs were summarized per reference with `samtools coverage` (samtools 1.21; @danecek2021) at a minimum mapping quality of 10. For each reference we recorded read count, covered bases, coverage breadth (fraction of the reference covered ≥1×) and mean depth. A reference was assigned to a sample when it satisfied both coverage breadth ≥ 0.10 (`hpv_min_coverage`) and mean depth ≥ 2 (`hpv_min_depth`); the full per-reference coverage table was retained regardless of assignment.

### Early/late transcript classification

To distinguish productive from non-productive infection, reads from each HPV-positive alignment were assigned to viral genes with featureCounts (subread ≥2.0; @liao2014) against the PaVE-derived gene annotation (`-t gene -g gene_name`, minimum overlap 20 nt, minimum mapping quality 10; pairing detected directly from the BAM and counted as read pairs when applicable). Per-gene counts were aggregated into an early total (E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7) and a late total (L1, L2). An infection was classified as productive when the L1 (major-capsid) read count reached the late-transcript threshold of 3 (`late_transcript_min_reads = 3`). Productivity was gated on L1 rather than on combined L1+L2 signal, since isolated L2 signal can arise from low-level transcription or cross-mapping.

### Cell-line, engineered, and contaminant flagging

Public RNA-seq is heavily populated by cancer cell lines, many carrying integrated HPV (e.g. HeLa/HPV18) that is a well-documented source of spurious HPV signal in archived data [@cantalupo2015; @kazemian2015]. Every sample was therefore annotated along three independent axes from its metadata, using a shared pattern library. The is_cell_line axis covers named lines such as HeLa, SiHa, CaSki, HaCaT and A431, plus generic markers like "cell line", "immortalized", "passage *n*", ATCC/DSMZ accessioning and PDX/xenograft. The is_engineered axis covers shRNA/siRNA/sgRNA, CRISPR/Cas9, transduction/transfection, lentiviral and plasmid-backbone constructs. The is_in_vitro axis covers cultured but non-immortalized material such as primary keratinocytes/fibroblasts/melanocytes, NHEK, organotypic/raft cultures, organoids and differentiation time-courses. Explicit "primary" annotations were treated as non-cell-line. These flags annotate rather than exclude samples, so that cell-line positives are retained as positive controls but can be separated from primary-tissue signal at analysis. For the prevalence-sweep cohort, study-level heuristic calls were additionally refined by manual curation through a structured workbook, with precedence sample > study > heuristic, and a provenance label recorded for each overridden call. As a further contaminant guard, low-coverage-breadth assignments (breadth < 0.15) and alpha-genus/HPV16/HPV18 calls were tabulated by study to surface project-level contamination.

### Sample groups and depth-normalized burden

Because lesional libraries may simply be sequenced more deeply than unselected skin, raw HPV read counts confound infection burden with sequencing depth. To neutralize this, every library that returned a Kraken2 report, including HPV-negative ones, was scored as papillomavirus reads per million (RPM), computed from the Kraken2 report as the Papillomaviridae clade read count divided by the sum of unclassified and root-level clade reads, times 10⁶. Samples were assigned to eight mutually exclusive sample groups. Seven follow from the metadata in fixed precedence: `cell_line` (any cell-line flag; *n* = `r comma(stats$cl2_n)`), `engineered` (knockdown, transgene or other manipulated culture; `r comma(stats$engt_n)`), `EV` (epidermodysplasia verruciformis diagnosis; `r comma(stats$ev_n)`), `control_productive` (wart/condyloma; `r comma(stats$ctrl_n)`), `neoplasia` (squamous/carcinoma/SCC/keratosis/Bowen; `r comma(stats$neo_n)`), `unselected_skin` (skin tissue; `r comma(stats$uns_n)`), and `other` (`r comma(stats$oth_n)`). The eighth, `non_permissive_tissue` (`r comma(stats$npt_n)`), cannot be read from a diagnosis field and was assigned study by study through the override table described below: cutaneous adipose tissue, blood cells and neural cells, none of which has a stratified squamous compartment. A further rule for pre-specified contaminated studies sits between `neoplasia` and `unselected_skin` in the code and matched no analyzed library.

### Metadata corrections

Because these rules read free-text metadata, they mis-file studies whose submitted fields are absent or misleading. Three such cases were found by inspecting every library that reached the detection floor, and corrected through an override table (`assets/tier_overrides.csv`) recording the accession, the corrected field and the evidence for each row. (i) A 10-library cohort of epidermodysplasia verruciformis skin biopsies [@saeidian2023] carries only `tissue=Skin`, so the diagnosis vocabulary never sees "verruciformis"; these were moved to `EV`, which otherwise held only immortalized EV *culture* models (retained under `cell_line`). (ii) Six libraries of HPV31-positive HaCaT (HaCaT31) cells expose only a knockdown label and `skin`, so no cell-line pattern can match; the cell-line flag was set. (iii) One primary cutaneous wart carried a submitter sample label in the SRA `cell_line` attribute; the flag was cleared, returning it to `control_productive`. Together these corrections move 16 of the 11,282 libraries carrying an RPM measurement. Running the pipeline with the override table disabled reproduces the uncorrected assignment exactly, and both outputs are retained. The same `is_cell_line` corrections are applied to the positivity model, so cell-line status is defined identically wherever it is used.

### Libraries excluded from the burden analysis

Two sets were excluded rather than regrouped, because neither a null nor a control describes them. First, 433 16S rRNA amplicon libraries, which carry no HPV sequence whatever the infection status and are therefore structural zeros rather than negative observations. Second, 15 libraries annotated `source_name=Skin or mucosa`, `tissue=adjacent mucosal tissues`, the matched adjacent tissue of 5 condyloma acuminatum donors sequenced as an RNA-seq library plus a MeRIP input and IP fraction each. Tissue taken millimeters from a productive lesion cannot separate independent infection from spillover out of it, and 5 donors in 3 fractions is one comparison rather than a population. Their lesions stay in `control_productive`, so neither the productive contrast nor the floor calibrated on it is affected. The analyzed cohort is `r comma(stats$n_burden)` libraries, of which `r comma(stats$n_both)` are also among the libraries screened in the sweep.

The two analyses are therefore fitted on different populations with different class definitions, and their counts are not interchangeable. The positivity model of @tbl-positivity uses the untargeted sweep alone, classed as clinical, engineered or cell-line material. The burden analysis pools that sweep with the targeted lesion cohorts, applies the two exclusions, and assigns the eight sample groups used elsewhere in the paper.

### Statistical analysis

A control-calibrated detection floor was defined as the 5th-percentile RPM of non-cell-line productive controls (warts/condyloma); libraries below it were considered "not detected at control level". To separate group differences from depth, the fraction of libraries at or above the floor was also computed within matched total-read bins (<5M, 5–10M, 10–20M, 20–40M, >40M). The same per-sample table yielded the HPV-type × sample-group catalog. Logistic-regression models (positivity by sample class; productive-level detection by sample group with a log~10~ sequencing-depth covariate) were fitted and Fisher exact tests run in R.

As a robustness check, the positivity, depth-controlled detection and productivity models were refitted as Bayesian logistic regressions in rstanarm [@rstanarm], with four Markov chains of 2,000 iterations (all R-hat ≤ 1.004, no divergent transitions) and weakly informative priors, Normal(0, 2.5) on the log-odds coefficients and Normal(0, 5) on the intercept. Effects are summarized by the posterior median odds ratio, its 95% credible interval, and the posterior probability of a positive effect; the near-separated productive-controls-versus-skin contrast was also checked under a heavier-tailed Student-*t*(3) prior (@supptbl-bayes).

### Library-selection chemistry

Chemistry was recovered for every library in the burden analysis. SRA RunInfo `LibrarySelection` was downloaded for the accession set already analyzed (`bin/fetch_library_selection.py`), and is the generic "cDNA" for `r pp(stats$chem_cdna_pct)`% of libraries: every library of the graded cervical series is labeled "cDNA" while its construction protocol reads "Ribosomal RNA was deleted". The free-text `LIBRARY_CONSTRUCTION_PROTOCOL` and `DESIGN_DESCRIPTION` records were therefore fetched in a second pass and matched against curated poly-A and rRNA-depletion phrase sets (`bin/classify_library_chemistry.py`). Libraries whose text supported both calls, or neither, were labeled "unspecified". Neither 3'-barcoded droplet libraries nor SMART template-switching is a selection chemistry, and both were coded as separate levels. This resolved chemistry for `r comma(stats$chem_n)` of `r comma(stats$chem_total)` libraries (`r pp(stats$chem_pct)`%).

### Integration status: E1:E2 transcript ratio and virus–host junctions

Libraries with at least 5 combined E1 and E2 reads were scored as
log~2~((E1 + 0.5)/(E2 + 0.5)) from the transcript classification already computed
for every library, and separation between groups was quantified as the area under
the ranked ratio and by Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

The ratio was validated against chimeric virus-host junctions in a subset of
`r stats$jx_n` libraries spanning its range. Reads were aligned with STAR
[@dobin2013] to a combined index of GRCh38 and the HPV reference panel with
chimeric detection enabled (`--chimSegmentMin 20`, `--chimJunctionOverhangMin 15`),
and a junction was retained when one side fell on an HPV contig and the other on a
human chromosome. Integration was scored by junction **clustering**, the fraction
of a library's junctions falling at its single most-supported coordinate pair,
rather than by junction count, which scales with viral depth. Observed values were bimodal with an empty interval between
`r stats$jx_epi_range` and `r stats$jx_int_range`, and a threshold of 0.2 was
placed within it. Integration was called in a library carrying as few as
`r comma(stats$jx_pos_minreads)` HPV reads, which bounds the viral depth at which
a negative call is informative.

The ratio was validated externally on a graded cervical series (BioProject
PRJNA612785, study SRP252916): HPV-negative normal epithelium, and
HPV16-positive normal epithelium, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion and
squamous carcinoma, six cases per arm by design, all paired-end and rRNA-depleted.
Of the HPV16-positive arms, `r stats$cxg_norm_n`, `r stats$cxg_hsil_n` and `r stats$cxg_scc_n` libraries
carried at least 5 viral gene reads, of which `r stats$cxg_norm_nr`, `r stats$cxg_hsil_nr` and `r stats$cxg_scc_nr` had the 5 E1 and E2 reads needed for a ratio (@fig-integration c). These libraries were typed and scored with the
same pipeline, criteria and thresholds as the skin cohort, with the study's own
design arms supplied in place of the group assignment
(`bin/e1e2_integration_marker.R --groups`), so the marker was evaluated against
labels it had no part in assigning. Single-cell and single-nucleus libraries are
excluded from the marker throughout, since 3'-biased barcoded coverage cannot
support a ratio across the early region.

### Independent DNA reservoir from public metagenomes

The presence data against which the transcriptional result is read come from a published petabase-scale papillomavirus catalog rather than from our own pipeline. Shen et al. screened the Logan assembly of 27 million archived sequencing libraries (Chikhi et al, 2024, bioRxiv preprint) for papillomavirus contigs, detecting the conserved L1 B and I domains by profile HMM and clustering the hits into operational types (Shen et al, 2026, eLife Reviewed Preprint). We re-tabulated their released cluster-by-library table by body site, bucketing libraries on the BioSample organism field into skin (`human skin metagenome`, `skin metagenome`), vaginal and gut metagenomes. The skin taxon also carries environmental transit surfaces and non-human animal skin, which were removed with a curated run exclusion list built from BioSample attributes (`bin/build_skin_run_exclusions.py`). Each contig cluster was mapped to an HPV type through the study's own taxonomy demarcation table and then to a genus through the same type-to-genus map used for our RNA catalogs, so the two modalities are labeled identically; a cluster whose papillomavirus identity resolves to no genus is reported as *Unresolved*, and one with no reference match as *Novel*.

All quantities from this catalog are compositions conditional on positivity: the denominator is the HPV-positive libraries of a body site, and a library carrying types of two genera contributes to both, so genus proportions within a site do not sum to one. No prevalence is computed, since a defensible denominator would require the screened-library count per body site to be reconstructed under the same freeze applied to the numerator. The type-level comparison joins the reservoir types onto both RNA catalogs, the assigned catalog (@supptbl-types) and the detection-level catalog (@supptbl-detection: at least 5 best-hit reads, MAPQ ≥ 20, and a majority of the library's primary alignments on that reference), so a type below the assignment threshold in skin RNA is reported as a detection-level call and never as an absence. This tabulation is implemented in `dna_rna_triangulation/shen_reservoir_by_tissue.R` and `dna_rna_triangulation/skin_dna_vs_rna_corrected.R`, and @fig-reservoir is built from their outputs by `manuscript/figure_reservoir.R`.
